caption_used: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive Reasoning. The Categorical pie chart comprises four segments: Universal Quantifiers (29.07%), Negation (27.91%), Limiter (27.91%), and Existential Quantifiers (15.12%). In the Approximate Number Generation chart, Comparative Relationships constitute the largest share at approximately 48%, followed by Approximate Quantities at 33.26% and Absolute Absence at 18.71%. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart shows a near-even split, with Conjunctive slightly dominating at 54.51% over Disjunctive at 45.49%.
raw_response: The figure presents three pie charts illustrating the distribution of different categories within reasoning tasks. The second pie chart, depicting Approximate Number Generation, consists of five segments: Comparative Relationships (blue, 36.26%), Approximate Quantities (light green, 45.03%), Absolute (yellow, 18.71%), Absence (orange, 18.71%), and Relationship (purple, 18.71%). The third pie chart, illustrating Disjunctive & Conjunctive reasoning, has two segments: Disjunctive (light red, 49.51%) and Conjunctive (yellow-orange, 50.49%). All three charts include percentage labels directly within each slice, and the segments appear ordered roughly in descending size within each chart. There is no legend provided.
